page: Amazon Web Services c6id.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 54 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance type bundles 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-thread execution alongside expected constraints in multi-core scalability due to its 2-core physical limit. The c6id.xlarge scores 1888.1 in stress-ng single-core tests and 1600.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, placing it in the average performance tier. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 28.1 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.18 GB/sec perform solidly. Multi-core throughput is more constrained, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 3413.0 and stress-ng multi-core recording 3863.16. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks tests at 29.55 GB/sec for reads and 24.58 GB/sec for writes, reflecting standard dual-channel DDR4 throughput.

From an architectural standpoint, bundling dedicated NVMe SSD local storage provides cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads that require low-latency scratch space without provisioning external EBS volumes. However, with only 8.0 GB of system memory, workloads are constrained from running memory-heavy in-memory datasets. Static web serving throughput reaches 6.41 GB/sec, and Redis operations register 3.86 million operations per second, establishing the instance as a practical fit for distributed web tier serving, batch compute processing, CI/CD worker nodes, and front-end caching requiring local temporary disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 3.5 GHz, the instance delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supplemented by 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It features a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD for fast local instance storage and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no GPU hardware present. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core computing capabilities, evidenced by average results in Geekbench single-core and gzip compression tests, while overall multi-threaded capacity reflects the two-core allocation. The integrated NVMe storage enhances resource efficiency for I/O-sensitive pipelines without external volume overhead. This configuration is particularly suited for microservices hosting, CI/CD runners, batch compute tasks, and static web serving.
